question.:question/problem: Given that $y =-\frac{3}{5}\ln x$, find the slope of the tangent at $x = 1$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the slope of the tangent at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

Taking the derivative, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}&=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-\frac{3}{5}\ln x) \\ &=-\frac{3}{5}\cdot\frac{1}{x} \\ &=-\frac{3}{5x}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent at $x=1$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\big|_{x=1}&=\left(- \frac{3}{5 x}\right)\big|_{x=1} \\ &=- \frac{3}{5}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3x-5+8{log}_{2}⁡x) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3x)+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-5)+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(8{log}_{2}⁡x) \\  & =3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x)-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(5)+8\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({log}_{2}⁡x) \\  & =3-0+8\cdot \frac{1}{xln⁡2} \\  & =3+\frac{8}{xln⁡2}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

To find the slope of the tangent at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

Taking the derivative, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3ln⁡x+2{x}^{2}-5x) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3ln⁡x)+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2{x}^{2})-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(5x) \\  & =3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(ln⁡x)+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2{x}^{2})-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(5x) \\  & =3\cdot \frac{1}{x}+4x-5 \\  & =\frac{3}{x}+4x-5\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent at $x=1$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=1} & ={(\frac{3}{x}+4x-5)|}_{x=1} \\  & =\frac{3}{1}+4\cdot 1-5 \\  & =3+4-5 \\  & =2\,.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Given that $y = \log_{3} x + 8\ln x$, find the slope of the tangent at $x = 1$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the slope of the tangent at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

Taking the derivative, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}&=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\log_{3}x+8\ln x) \\ &=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\log_{3}x)+8\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\ln x) \\ &=\frac{1}{x\ln 3}+\frac{8}{x}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent at $x=1$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\big|_{x=1}&=\left(\frac{1}{x \ln{\left(3 \right)}} + \frac{8}{x}\right)\big|_{x=1} \\ &=\frac{1}{\ln{\left(3 \right)}} + 8\,.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Given that $y=2{e}^{x}-10{log}_{5}x$, find the slope of the tangent at $x=3.$

{{field-1}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the slope of the tangent at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

Taking the derivative, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=2{e}^{x}-\frac{10}{x\operatorname{ln}5}\,.
$$

Therefore, the slope  of the tangent at $x=3$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=3} & ={(2{e}^{x}-\frac{10}{x\operatorname{ln}5})|}_{x=3} \\  & =2{e}^{3}-\frac{10}{3\operatorname{ln}5} \\  & =2{e}^{3}-\frac{\frac{10}{3}}{\operatorname{ln}5}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the slope of the tangent at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

Taking the derivative, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3{x}^{3}-10{log}_{3}⁡x) \\  & =3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{3})-10\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({log}_{3}⁡x) \\  & =3\cdot 3{x}^{2}-10\cdot \frac{1}{xln⁡3} \\  & =9{x}^{2}-\frac{10}{xln⁡3}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent at $x=1$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=1} & ={(9{x}^{2}-\frac{10}{xln⁡3})|}_{x=1} \\  & =9(1)^{2}-\frac{10}{1ln⁡3} \\  & =9-\frac{10}{1ln⁡3}\,.\end{aligned}
$$
